newsitem.title: UK: RJB Mining to close central England mine.
newsitem.headline: RJB Mining to close central England mine.

text.p: Britain's RJB Mining said on Monday it would close down its Asfordby coal mine in north east Leicestershire in central England following adverse geological conditions.
Production has already ceased at the site and RJB said most of the 490 employees would be offered transfers to other mines in the Midlands and South Yorkshire.
"However, a small number of compulsory redundancies are likely," the company said.
It said it had adequate alternative sources of coal to supply Asfordby's customers.

The mines have been suffering a series of volcanic sills which lie above the coal seams, causing unusual and inconsistent fracturing patterns, resulting in severe damage to face equipment and inflow of water.
"Despite attempts at alternative systems of mining involving shorter length faces, these conditions have persisted," it said.
In 1995 the colliery made an operating loss of 16.3 million stg and in 1996 it stood at 19.9 million stg. The colliery, however, made a small profit in the first six months of 1997.
The cost of closing Asfordby would be met by existing provisions, the company said.
